---
title: Live stream (SSE)
description: Follow each resolution stage as it completes with server-sent events from /v1/stream.
---

import { Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import CaseDiagram from '../../../components/CaseDiagram.astro';
import Flow from '../../../components/Flow.astro';

`GET /v1/stream/{did}` resolves a DID like [`/v1/resolve`](/build/resolution/), but sends each stage as a server-sent event as soon as it finishes: parsing the DID, DNS, the HTTPS fetch, domain linkage and so on. Use it to show progress in a UI, or to see where a slow or failing resolution stops.

The final result is the **same resolution** as `/v1/resolve`. The stream adds timing and order; it does not add any other evidence.

<CaseDiagram
  label="Your client opens an event stream; DID.is resolves the DID and sends each stage as it completes"

/>

## Event order

<Flow
  label="Order of server-sent events"
  steps={[
    { title: 'stage', body: 'One event per completed stage, in order.', code: 'event: stage' },
    { title: 'result or error', body: 'The full resolution, or an RFC 9457 problem.', code: 'event: result' },
    { title: 'done', body: 'The stream ends.', code: 'event: done' },
  ]}
/>

## What you get

- **Each stage** with `stage`, `label`, `status`, `startedUs`, `durationUs` and `detail`. The same stages appear in the `trace` array of `/v1/resolve`.
- **The full resolution** in the `result` event, same shape as `/v1/resolve`.

## What it does not tell you

- **Anything the resolution does not.** The stream reports the same evidence with the same [limits](/build/resolution/#what-is-not-checked).
- **Fresh network stages for a cached result.** Without `?noCache=true`, a cached result shows a `cache.hit` stage instead of the DNS and fetch stages. The SDKs stream with `noCache` by default.

## Request

The endpoint uses the intensive budget (10 requests per minute). See [Errors and rate limits](/build/errors/).

<Tabs syncKey="lang">
<TabItem label="curl">
```bash
curl -N 'https://did.is/api/v1/stream/did:web:did.is?noCache=true'
```
</TabItem>
<TabItem label="TypeScript">
```ts
import { DidisClient } from "@didis/client";

const didis = new DidisClient();
for await (const ev of didis.stream("did:web:did.is")) {
  if (ev.event === "stage") console.log(ev.data.status, ev.data.label);
  if (ev.event === "result") console.log(ev.data.verdict.headline);
  if (ev.event === "error") console.error(ev.data.code, ev.data.detail);
}
```
</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Python">
```python
from didis import DidisClient

with DidisClient() as didis:
    for event, data in didis.stream("did:web:did.is"):
        if event == "stage":
            print(data["status"], data["label"])
        elif event == "result":
            print(data["verdict"]["headline"])
        elif event == "error":
            print(data.get("code"), data.get("detail"))
```
</TabItem>
</Tabs>

The SDKs resolve fresh (`noCache`) by default when streaming and stop after `done`. Pass `{ noCache: false }` / `no_cache=False` to accept a cached result.

Start of a live stream (`detail` lines shortened):

```text
event: stage
data: {"stage":"syntax.parse","label":"DID syntax (DID Core §3.1)","status":"PASS","startedUs":0,"durationUs":3,"detail":"method 'web' · 14 characters"}

event: stage
data: {"stage":"method.web.transform","label":"DID-to-HTTPS transformation","status":"PASS","startedUs":6,"durationUs":9,"detail":"did:web:did.is → https://did.is/.well-known/did.json"}

event: stage
data: {"stage":"egress.dns","label":"DNS resolution and address pinning","status":"PASS","startedUs":28,"durationUs":1629,"detail":"did.is pinned to 104.21.76.195 (all answers public)"}

event: stage
data: {"stage":"egress.fetch","label":"TLS handshake and HTTP exchange","status":"PASS","startedUs":1779,"durationUs":42936,"detail":"GET https://did.is/.well-known/did.json → HTTP 200 · 678 bytes; …"}

…

event: stage
data: {"stage":"evidence.assemble","label":"Evidence assembly","status":"PASS","startedUs":89080,"durationUs":125,"detail":"7 dimensions · 7 graph nodes · verdict RESOLVED"}

event: result
data: { …full resolution… }

event: done
data: {}
```

## Reading the result

| Stage `status` | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| `PASS` | The stage completed and its check passed. |
| `FAIL` | The stage failed. An `error` event usually follows with the problem. |
| `WARN` | The stage completed with a finding worth reading in `detail`. |
| `INFO` | Information only, for example `cache.hit`. |

| Final event | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `result` | Read it like a [`/v1/resolve` result](/build/resolution/#reading-the-result). |
| `error` | Handle the problem `code` as on [Errors and rate limits](/build/errors/). |

If the request is refused before the stream starts (for example `429`), you receive a normal problem response instead of an event stream.
